idiom_name: Result-matching receiver + basic_nack(requeue = false) / produce to an error topic (lapin, rdkafka)
implementation_notes: No Rust framework owns the invalid channel: deserialization is a Result (serde, prost or a hand-rolled decoder) and the receiver matches on it to choose between handling and diverting. With lapin the invalid path is Acker::basic_nack with requeue = false, which lets RabbitMQ dead-letter the delivery according to the queue's policy; with rdkafka the raw payload is produced to an error topic before the offset is committed, because Kafka has no broker-side dead-lettering. The classic structure is worth keeping because the routing decision is a typed match over error kinds and because ownership forces the original bytes to be captured while the delivery is still alive.
pitfalls: basic_nack without requeue = false returns the payload to the same queue and reproduces the poison loop.
Acknowledging before the error-topic produce is confirmed loses the only copy of the invalid payload; publish (and wait for the acknowledgement) first.
Borrowing the delivery buffer across an await while the delivery is dropped at ack time is a use-after-free waiting to happen - the diverted copy must own its bytes.
